h1: The 6 Best Small Safes With Keys of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Safes With Keys 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 small key-lock safes, from fire-rated SentrySafe boxes to budget steel boxes, compared on fire rating, mounting and keys.
summary: The SentrySafe fireproof chest with bolt-down hardware is the best key-lock safe for most homes, combining a UL fire classification, two keys and a low price tier. A second SentrySafe adds a lifetime replacement guarantee, a third holds hanging files, and three plain steel boxes cover cash and medication.
intro: A key lock never runs out of battery, which is its quiet advantage over keypad safes. Its weak point is the key itself. The classic mistake is stashing the spare key inside the safe it opens, which turns a backup into a lockout. Plan where the keys live before you buy the box.

We reviewed six key lock safes from the listings and ranked them on fire classification, mounting, included keys and extra protection. Prices run from under $25 to $100. Fire ratings are stated by the makers and classifiers named in each listing, not something we verified ourselves.

products.name: SentrySafe Fireproof Safe with Key Lock, Chest Lock Box for Home or Travel
products.verdict: UL fire classification plus bolt-down hardware.
products.description:
This SentrySafe is a flat key lock chest with a UL Classified rating of one half hour at 1550 degrees F, bolt-down hardware, a carrying handle and two keys, all in the $25 to $50 tier. It covers the basics for documents and small valuables in a single low cost box.

It leads because it is the only box here that pairs a fire classification with mounting hardware at that price. The second SentrySafe chest has a lifetime replacement guarantee but lists no mounting hardware, so it can be carried away. Bonsaii and Yuanshikj mount but offer no fire protection.

Buy it for passports, deeds and spare cash. The caveat is that a half hour rating is a baseline, not extreme protection, and the interior is small.

products.name: SentrySafe Fireproof Safe Box with Key Lock, Chest Safe with Carrying Handle
products.description:
The second SentrySafe chest is also UL Classified at one half hour at 1550 degrees F, and its key lock is described as holding the lid shut during a fire. It adds a lifetime after fire replacement guarantee and two keys, but our data shows no price bucket.

It ranks second because it lists no mounting hardware, so it relies on a carrying handle and can be lifted by a thief. Against the first SentrySafe, you gain the replacement guarantee and lose the bolt-down option.

Buy it if the after fire guarantee matters to you and the chest will sit somewhere hard to reach, such as a closet shelf. Skip it if you want the box fixed to the floor. The honest caveat is that it is easy to carry off, which limits its theft protection.
products.skipIf: You want to bolt it down.

products.name: SentrySafe Black Fireproof and Waterproof Safe, File Folder and Document Box
products.verdict: Hanging file capacity with fire and water protection.
products.description:
This SentrySafe holds hanging file folders and lists UL Classified fire protection plus ETL Verified water protection, with a key lock and two keys. It carries a $50 to $100 price tag.

Third place is justified since it costs more than the chest safes, but it adds the file capacity and the water protection that they do not list. If your paperwork lives in manila folders, that matters more than a bolt-down kit.

It is the right choice for households keeping tax records, insurance papers and family documents together. Skip it if you only store cash and small items, since the larger body is wasted. The caveat is size and price: it is bulkier than the 0.23 cubic foot boxes below and takes more shelf space.

products.name: Bonsaii Security Safe Box with Key Lock, 0.23 Cu.Ft for Cash Jewelry Home
products.verdict: A mountable steel box with hidden hinges.
products.description:
The Bonsaii is a 0.23 cubic foot steel box with a flat key lock, a pry resistant door and hidden hinges, in the $25 to $50 tier. It can be mounted, and the listing gives clear guidance on where to keep the spare key.

It ranks fourth because it lists no fire rating, which puts it behind the SentrySafe boxes for documents. For cash and jewelry, the hidden hinges and the pry resistant door are the meaningful features, and it costs about the same as the lead pick.

It suits valuables that are mainly at risk from theft rather than fire. Skip it if paper documents are the main contents. The caveat is the small interior, which fits a few items and not much else.

products.name: Yuanshikj Steel Small Safe Lock Box with Key Security, 0.23 Cu Ft, Black
products.verdict: 2 keys and wall, floor or cabinet mounting.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj is a 0.23 cubic foot steel box with a flat key lock and two unique keys, rated in the under $25 tier. The listing says it can mount to a wall, floor or cabinet or be used as a portable box, and the powder coating resists scratches and stains.

It ranks fifth because it has no fire rating, but it also costs the least. Against the Bonsaii, it matches the capacity and adds flexible mounting while giving up the hidden hinge detail.

Buy it for budget cash storage or to keep small items away from children. Skip it if you want fire protection. The honest caveat is a thin feature list, so this is a simple lock box rather than a serious security product.

products.name: KYODOLED Small Metal Lock Box with Key for Cash and Medication, 2 Keys
products.verdict: A two-layer portable box with a coin tray.
products.description:
The KYODOLED is a portable metal lock box with two keys, a two layer design and a removable five compartment coin tray, in the under $25 tier. It has a built in carry handle.

It ranks last because it is built for organization more than security against theft. Compared with the Yuanshikj, it cannot be mounted, and it has no fire rating to offset that.

It suits medication, small cash and coins that need to stay away from kids or guests in the house. Skip it if you want real protection against a determined thief. The caveat is simple: it is portable by design, so anyone can pick it up and leave with it, locked or not.

methodology.title: Fire classification
methodology.description: UL classified ratings counted heavily, as claims without a classification were treated as unverified.

methodology.title: Extras
methodology.description: Water protection and file capacity counted as extras.

whatMatters.detail: A fire classification is a lab rating naming a time and temperature, such as one half hour at 1550 degrees F. It matters because marketing words like fireproof prove nothing without a named standard. Look for UL or another classifier and the numbers in the listing, as the SentrySafe boxes show.

Mounting hardware lets you fix the safe to a floor, wall or cabinet. It matters because a small safe that can be carried away is only a delay for a thief. Look for included bolts and pre-drilled holes, not just the word mountable, as the first SentrySafe and Yuanshikj list.

Key count and spare plan: a key lock needs at least two keys, and the spare should live somewhere else. It matters because a lost sole key can mean drilling the lock. Look for two keys included, and decide on a hiding place before you fill the box.

Water protection is a separate rating from fire, often ETL Verified. It matters for floods, burst pipes and sprinkler discharge, which can ruin documents even when no fire occurs. Check which standard the listing names, as the file box does, and note that most boxes here list none.

Size and layout cover interior dimensions and compartments. A deeper box suits cash and jewelry, while a file box holds hanging folders. Check the listed capacity in cubic feet, like the 0.23 on the Bonsaii and Yuanshikj, and compare it with what you actually plan to store.

faq.a: No. A key lock has nothing to power, which is its main advantage over keypad models. The trade is that you must keep track of the keys, ideally two, stored apart from the safe itself.
Storing the spare key inside the safe. If you lock the only keys in, the box becomes useless. Bonsaii even gives explicit spare key guidance, so follow it or hide one elsewhere.

faq.q: Is a UL fire rating worth it?
faq.a: For documents, yes. A UL classification like the SentrySafe chest names a tested time and temperature. The Bonsaii and Yuanshikj list no fire rating, so they fit cash and jewelry better than paper.

faq.q: How do I mount a small safe?
faq.a: Use the included bolts through the pre-drilled holes into a stud or floor. The first SentrySafe ships with bolt-down hardware, and the Yuanshikj can mount to a wall, floor or cabinet according to its listing.

faq.q: How do I maintain a key lock?
faq.a: Keep keys dry and use the lock occasionally so it keeps moving. A drop of lock lubricant now and then helps the SentrySafe or KYODOLED lock, and always test both keys after any move.

The KYODOLED and the SentrySafe chests have handles, so they can travel. They are not theft proof, though, because anyone can carry them off. Use the KYODOLED for medication in transit and keep valuables bolted down at home.

finalTake: For documents, buy a fire classified SentrySafe and bolt it down. The file box suits paper heavy households, while Bonsaii and Yuanshikj are fine for cash and jewelry that fire is unlikely to threaten. Treat the KYODOLED as an organizer rather than a security product, and keep every spare key outside the safe.
